title: Automatic Large Language Models Creation of Interactive Learning Lessons
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether large language models can automatically generate scenario-based interactive lessons for training novice human tutors. The central question is whether an LLM-based, retrieval-augmented workflow can produce tutor-training lessons that are comparable in quality to those written by expert lesson designers, and how the level of prompt decomposition affects output quality.

The intervention studied is a lesson-generation pipeline that combines retrieval-augmented generation with GPT-4o and task decomposition prompting. The authors generated English lessons for three tutor-training topics: encouraging students’ independence, encouraging help-seeking behavior, and turning on cameras. Each lesson followed a five-part structure: title page, scenario 1, instruction, scenario 2, and conclusion. The main experimental factor was how the lesson was split across prompts, ranging from one segment to five segments.

The context is online tutor training for novice human tutors teaching middle school mathematics. Rather than testing student learning directly, the paper evaluated generated lessons with two experienced human raters and then compared the best-performing LLM-generated lessons with human-crafted lessons through feedback from two lesson designers. The study found that a three-segment decomposition performed best overall, outperforming a single-step prompt and slightly outperforming more granular decompositions. Human evaluators and lesson designers saw clear benefits such as time savings, realistic scenario generation, and useful instructional charts, but they also identified recurring problems including generic feedback, unclear learning objectives, logical disconnects in instruction, and unreliable or fabricated references. The authors conclude that LLMs are promising for draft lesson creation, but human review remains necessary to ensure pedagogical quality and citation authenticity.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family large language model system used for generating and evaluating educational text and other content.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13) in a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to automatically generate scenario-based tutor-training lessons for middle school mathematics.

findings.finding_summary: Human evaluators rated the three-segment prompting approach highest for lesson quality (average rating 14.67) compared with one-segment generation (average 10.67). The paper reports that decomposing lesson generation into multiple subtasks improved overall quality of the LLM-generated tutor-training lessons.
findings.sample_size: n=3 lessons generated per segmentation approach

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods study with human ratings and designer feedback, not a controlled student-outcome experiment. The methodology is structured, but the evidence is not causal and does not report inferential effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports a clear improvement in rubric scores for decomposed prompting, but the effect is not expressed as a standardized effect size and is based on only three lessons per condition. Impact on learner outcomes remains untested, so practical impact is suggestive rather than established.
